transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s elevators. I know that sounds kind of silly, because I know they’re not really dangerous, people ride them all day, like at job sites and hospitals and whatever. My cousin used to work in one of those big office buildings downtown, and she’d take them constantly, no problem.

But when I have to get in one, I just get scared like I’m gonna be trapped in there, and I can’t make myself feel normal about it. Like my brain knows one thing, but my body doesn’t listen.
Do you get this same kind of fear in other places where it might be hard to get out quickly, like buses, trains, crowded stores, or theaters?

Um… I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve been on buses before and it’s not like I love them, but I don’t think it’s the same thing. Crowded stores can be annoying, like especially after work when everybody’s in the way and I’m tired, but that’s more just… people being everywhere, you know?

The elevator thing is the one that sticks in my head. Like if somebody says, “Just take the elevator,” that’s when I start thinking about it. I haven’t really noticed it the same way with theaters or trains or stuff like that.
When you get into an elevator, do you ever suddenly have a panic attack?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if it’s like a full panic attack or whatever you’d call it, but as soon as the doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight and my hands get sweaty, and I’m just thinking, I need to get out. Even if it’s only a couple floors.

It’s weird because I’ll be on a job site and I can handle loud equipment and all that, but that little box closing up just—yeah, it hits me right away.
Do you avoid elevators because of this fear?

Yeah, I do. I mean, not like I never ever get in one, but most days I’ll take the stairs, like at our apartment or on a job site. Which is kind of annoying because after hauling stuff all day, stairs are not exactly fun, but I still do it.

If the elevator or one of those lifts is the only way up, I’ll try to get put on different work if I can. Or I’ll ride it, but usually only if somebody I trust is right there with me. Like I don’t want to be in there by myself.
When you’re in an elevator, is the scariest part that escape or help might not be available if you panic?

Yeah… I think so. It’s more like, once I’m in there, I start thinking if it stops or something, I’m just stuck in that little space and I can’t get out. And I know, like, elevators are used all day, they’re probably fine — I’m not saying it makes sense.

It’s just my body doesn’t care about that. I’ve worked around way more dangerous stuff, honestly, and then this stupid elevator in an office building gets to me. Like I start feeling like I’m trapped, and I can’t make myself just be normal about it.
Have you ever had one of these panic episodes come on out of the blue, when you weren’t in or about to get into an elevator?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, not like that.

I get worked up about plenty of things, like if work’s running behind or somebody’s yelling on site — people get all heated over dumb stuff sometimes — but that’s different. The elevator thing feels very specific, like it starts when I’m right there or thinking I have to get in. I can’t really remember it just hitting me out of nowhere while I’m sitting at home or anything.
Besides elevators, are there other places where you avoid going because you feel like you might be trapped and unable to get out?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. Like, I don’t sit there making a list of places I can’t go or anything.

I mean, there’s places I don’t like, sure — like if a job site is all jammed up and everybody’s in everybody’s way, that gets on my nerves. And some stores, you know, with the aisles packed and people stopping right in front of you like they forgot how walking works… but that’s more irritating than scary.

The trapped feeling, that’s mostly the elevator thing. I can’t think of another place I avoid like that.
Do you feel this same trapped fear in any other enclosed spaces, like tunnels or small rooms?

Not really, no. I mean, small rooms can be annoying if there’s too much junk in there, like on a job when somebody stacks materials where you’re trying to work — that drives me nuts — but it’s not the same.

The thing I’m here about is really elevators. I know they’re not actually dangerous, like I’m not dumb, I know people use them all day. But when I have to get in one, I get scared like I’m gonna be trapped in there and I can’t make myself feel normal about it.
